hoods.Downtown: The SpeedyBurger line snakes out the door at lunchtime, and the sidewalks feel busier than ever with people rushing between meetings. Rents keep climbing, and you overhear neighbors talking about how they're stretching their budgets to stay.
hoods.Temescal: The Temescal Community Health Center buzzes with activity as patients come and go. At Da Dough, the smell of fresh pizza draws a steady stream of customers.
hoods.Laurel: MacArthur Kitchen stays busy with families grabbing dinner after school events. A neighbor keeps coming up in conversations around town, but no one can quite place why.
hoods.West Oakland: Block parties spill onto the streets, with music and laughter echoing through the industrial flats. Seniors gather for lunch at the New Covenant Pentecostal Assembly, celebrating a program milestone.
hoods.Fruitvale: Job seekers file into a workshop at St. Esperanza Parish, eager to start the new training session. The Fruitvale Transit Hub buzzes with activity as planners meet to discuss Phase II.
hoods.Jack London: The sidewalks are packed every evening with young professionals heading to waterfront bars and restaurants. Rent signs keep popping up on older buildings, with prices that make longtime residents shake their heads. A few moving trucks are spotted on side streets as some families decide to relocate.
hoods.Rockridge: The food pantry at Temple Beth Or sees a steady stream of neighbors picking up groceries. On the corner, an Oakland Alternative Response Initiative team calmly handles a situation without fanfare.
hoods.Adams Point: Vernon Street Market bustles with shoppers grabbing fresh produce. Adams Point United Methodist Church seems quieter than usual after losing two employees.
hoods.Grand Lake: A job training workshop kicks off at Or Hashalom Renewal Community, drawing hopeful participants. Residents chat about feeling safer lately, crediting the Oakland Alternative Response Initiative.
hoods.Piedmont Ave: The food pantry at B'nai Tikvah Synagogue serves neighbors in need, with volunteers working efficiently. A boutique corner offers a quiet respite, with last summer's hit song drifting from a car stereo.
hoods.Chinatown: The Oakland Asian Cultural Center stays busy with classes and events. A neighbor keeps coming up in conversations around town, but no one can quite place why.
